stories.headline: Tensions Rise Between US and Iran as Trump Threatens Oman
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump has threatened to bomb Oman if the nation interferes with American negotiations with Iran, according to a report by Fox News [c4]. The threat comes at a time of severe tension across the Middle East as military actions expand [c4, c10].

In Iraq, violent attacks have directly targeted political and security leaders [c10]. Two Hadid-110 drones launched from Iranian territory struck the office of Kurdistan Regional Government Prime Minister Masrour Barzani, as well as the residence of a regional security chief [c10]. United States Ambassador to Iraq Tom Barrack strongly condemned these drone strikes in Iraqi Kurdistan, calling them a direct threat to regional stability [c11].

At the diplomatic level, statements from officials remain conflicted [c6, c7]. A spokesperson for the Iranian news agency Tasnim publicly denied President Donald Trump's claim that the United States maintains a direct backchannel with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps [c7]. However, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei stated that Iran and Oman have reached an understanding on transit route maps through the strategic Strait of Hormuz [c6]. The passage is vital for global energy supplies, as approximately one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas passes through the Strait of Hormuz [c5].

The ongoing conflict is causing significant economic impact both in the Middle East and inside the United States [c2, c8, c9]. Hotel occupancy in Dubai fell drastically from 80 percent to around 10 percent after Iran launched strikes against allies of the United States in response to previous US-Israel attacks [c8]. In response to the crisis, the United Arab Emirates introduced a $680 million economic package to support local businesses affected by the Iran war [c9]. Meanwhile, consumers in the United States are facing higher costs, as US gasoline prices rose by nearly a third compared to one year earlier, according to the American Automobile Association [c2].

These developments coincide with rising domestic political pressure on the American administration [c1, c3]. A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll found that 80 percent of Americans believe that US involvement in Iran will continue for an extended period [c3]. The same Reuters/Ipsos poll showed that President Donald Trump's approval rating has dropped to 33 percent, which matches the lowest point of his presidency [c1].

vocab.meaning: involves oneself in a matter without right or invitation
the proportion of used or rented rooms in a building or hotel

stories.headline: Trump Orders Scale-Back of US Military Drills in South Korea
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump has announced on Truth Social that the United States will substantially reduce its joint military exercises with South Korea [c14]. Trump explicitly linked this decision to scale back the joint drills to South Korea's refusal to assist in American military operations regarding Iran [c15]. Approximately 28,500 American military personnel are currently stationed in South Korea [c16].

Despite President Trump's order to reduce the exercises, joint military drills between South Korea and the United States proceeded as scheduled on Monday [c18]. In response to the announcement, South Korea's presidential Blue House stated that it would review Donald Trump's comments while continuing diplomatic consultations with Washington [c17].

The military policy shift follows other diplomatic remarks made by the US president [c12, c13]. Speaking in the Oval Office, Donald Trump stated that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un responded positively to his diplomatic overtures [c12]. Meanwhile, US envoy Jared Kushner stated that progress toward Gaza demilitarization could materialize in as little as 30 days [c13].

vocab.meaning: to a large or significant degree
approaches or proposals made to establish a relationship or agreement

stories.headline: Gaza Ceasefire Talks Stall as Kushner Meets Regional Leaders
stories.body:
US envoy Jared Kushner has left Jerusalem without reaching a breakthrough after holding two days of diplomatic talks with Israeli and Hamas leaders [c22]. Before travelling to Jerusalem, Kushner met with Hamas political chief Khalil al-Hayya in Egypt [c26]. Despite the lack of a major deal, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Jared Kushner agreed that an American general will oversee the disarmament of Hamas in Gaza [c19]. They also agreed to establish specialized working groups focused on Gaza's demilitarization and public health [c23].

The diplomatic efforts take place as violence and political tension persist [c20, c24, c25]. Israeli military forces currently control approximately 60 percent of the Gaza Strip [c20]. Gaza's health ministry reported that at least 1,265 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli military operations since the ceasefire went into effect on October 10 [c25]. Meanwhile, far-right Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir stated in a podcast interview that Israel should kill 30 to 40 people every night in Gaza [c24].

International criticism of Israel's stance has grown [c21]. Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Pakistan, and Indonesia issued a joint statement condemning Israel's rejection of the US-backed ceasefire proposal [c21].

vocab.meaning: the reduction or withdrawal of military weapons and forces

stories.headline: European Nations Deploy Emergency Support Amid Severe Wildfires
stories.body:
Wildfires and intense heatwaves are causing severe damage across Europe, leading to international emergency deployments [c31, c33, c35]. Data from the European Forest Fire Information System revealed that 576,000 hectares of land burned across Europe in 2026 [c35]. The EU's Copernicus service confirmed that western Europe experienced its warmest June-to-July period on record [c33].

Tragedies and evacuations have been reported in several countries [c27, c29, c30, c36]. In Spain, a Spanish soldier died while battling the Peñas de Riglos wildfire in the Aragón region [c30]. In Greece, two people died and hundreds were evacuated due to twin wildfires on the island of Salamina [c29]. In Germany, approximately 30 residents in the border town of Monschau received evacuation orders as High Fens wildfires approached [c36]. In France, 183 homes were destroyed in Le Porge, where French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu was heckled by residents during a visit [c27]. Lecornu announced €12 million in government aid for the Gironde and Landes regions [c28].

European nations are sending aid to affected neighbors [c31, c32, c34]. Britain deployed military personnel to assist across Europe [c31]. France sent 104 firefighters and 36 emergency vehicles to Spain [c32], while Germany, Sweden, Norway, and the Netherlands sent emergency aerial and ground reinforcements to Belgium [c34].

vocab.meaning: interrupted a speaker with aggressive or taunting comments
extra personnel or equipment sent to support a military or emergency force

stories.headline: Ebola Epidemic in Democratic Republic of Congo Becomes Deadliest Ever
stories.body:
An ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed 2,325 people, making it the country's deadliest Ebola epidemic on record [c37]. The DRC Public Health Institute reported that total confirmed Ebola cases reached 4,945, with 101 new cases detected in just 24 hours [c38]. More than 3,400 of these confirmed cases were recorded in the DRC's Ituri province [c39].

While the Democratic Republic of Congo battles the crisis, neighboring Uganda declared itself free of Ebola on July 28 after discharging its final treated patient [c40].

International health organizations and medical researchers are working on vaccines to combat the disease [c41, c42]. World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stated that two vaccines developed specifically for the Bundibugyo strain are currently undergoing clinical trials [c41]. Additionally, the UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency granted approval for human trials of an Oxford University-developed vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo Ebola strain [c42].

vocab.meaning: a widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a community at a particular time
a particular type or genetic variant of a biological virus or organism

stories.headline: Deadly 7.7-Magnitude Earthquake Strikes Eastern Indonesia
stories.body:
A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck eastern Indonesia shortly before 06:00 local time on Saturday, leaving at least 68 people dead and over 200 others injured [c43, c47]. The quake hit Flores island at a depth of 15 kilometers [c47]. The surrounding East Nusa Tenggara province registered nearly 1,600 aftershocks following the major tremor [c44].

The destruction from the earthquake has caused widespread displacement and strain on medical services [c45, c46, c48]. The disaster damaged more than 900 buildings and forced nearly 13,000 people from their homes [c48]. On Flores island, Dr. Melinda, the sole physician at the Dampek Health Centre, issued an urgent plea for help while treating hundreds of quake victims [c46]. During the crisis, a woman named Maria Florida Nogo Kelen underwent emergency C-section surgery to give birth as the earthquake struck [c45].

vocab.meaning: the forced movement of people from their home area
an involuntary shaking movement or a slight earthquake

stories.headline: BJP Announces Major Leadership Overhaul Under President Nitin Nabin
stories.body:
The Bharatiya Janata Party has announced a major national organizational reshuffle under President Nitin Nabin, replacing nearly 50 of the 65 office-bearers on its national team [c53, c56]. The broad reorganization includes 12 women leaders in the newly announced national leadership team [c53].

As part of the reshuffle, former Union minister Smriti Irani was appointed as a BJP national general secretary and placed in charge of Uttar Pradesh [c51, c55]. This appointment follows political challenges in the state during recent elections [c52]. The party's vote share in Uttar Pradesh dropped significantly from around 50 percent in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections to approximately 41 percent in 2024 [c52].

Smriti Irani is one of eight leaders appointed as national general secretaries [c55]. The other newly named national general secretaries are Biplab Deb, Sunil Bansal, Vinod Tawde, Gajendra Patel, Satish Poonia, Harish Dwivedi, and Sanjay Bhatia [c55]. In another major appointment, Professor Tariq Mansoor, the former vice chancellor of Aligarh Muslim University, was named a BJP national vice president [c54].

The party also made significant changes to its digital operations [c49, c50]. Deepak Mhaskey was appointed as the BJP's new national social media convener, taking over the role from his long-serving predecessor Amit Malviya [c49]. Mhaskey previously worked as a college chemistry professor and served as the head of the BJP social media cell in the state of Chhattisgarh [c50].

vocab.meaning: a reorganization of positions within a political party or organization
a person who held a job or office before the current holder
a person who brings a group together or manages a specific section

stories.headline: Jharkhand Cancels Recruitment Exams Following Widespread Student Protests
stories.body:
Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren has announced the cancellation of the JSSC-CGL recruitment examination and all official activities associated with the testing agency TDPL [c59]. Following the announcement, student leader Devendra Nath Mahto ended his hunger strike after Chief Minister Soren agreed to cancel the disputed recruitment exams [c57].

The decision followed intense student demonstrations across the state capital of Ranchi [c58, c63]. Protesting students organized under the JPSC-JSSC Abhyarthi Nyay Manch and JPSC-JSSC Reform Manch platforms held sit-in protests at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, where six students went on an indefinite hunger strike [c58, c63]. National political support also emerged when Congress leader Rahul Gandhi sent a letter to CM Hemant Soren, urging him to meet directly with the demonstrating students [c62].

In response to the protests and examination irregularities, the Jharkhand government ordered a comprehensive CID investigation into recruitment exam errors occurring since 2014 [c60]. Additionally, the state government decided to form a dedicated examination reforms committee headed by senior IAS officer Amitabh Kaushal [c61].

vocab.meaning: subject to disagreement, argument, or debate
acts or events that do not conform to proper rules or standards
